title: Yvonne S NDE 5185
content: I was in the hospital for outpatient surgery on my toe. I was (am) in good health and no problems were anticipated. During my recovery, when the breathing tube was removed, I was not able to breathe. When I had woken up, the recovery nurse was very close to my ear, telling me to breathe. I tried to tell her that I couldn't breathe, but no sound came out. She kept telling me to breathe and I kept trying to tell her that breathing was not possible. In my head, I started yelling at the nurse, telling her that if I COULD breathe, I WOULD and STOP telling me to breathe. Then it occurred to me that I was going to die, and I thought, 'This can't be happening. I'm not ready, and my daughter is waiting in recovery. I can't die over a silly little toe procedure.' It struck me as ironic, and at the same time aggravating, that this was happening to me, and that these people seemed like a bunch of idiots - especially the nurse who was getting on my nerves with her insistence that I breathe. Why couldn't she tell that I was struggling to breathe, but it just wasn't working? Soon after, my legs started shaking and then my whole body. I wondered why my body was bouncing around, but it didn't hurt and it was a pleasant distraction. Suddenly I was aware that I was looking down on my body - but I could also feel. I saw it (my body) bouncing, and it felt like I was on a washing machine and that something else was bouncing me around. So, now I'm somewhere around the ceiling looking down at my body on the table. That was when I noticed all the people in the room. They were doing things quickly, crowding around the table and me. A guy went to the speaker on the wall and said, 'Code red!' and then called for my chest x-rays. From my place near the ceiling, I answered him. I told him that they didn't have my chest x-rays, because they hadn't taken any. But he did not appear to hear me. After that, everything went black. I woke up while being transferred to a hospital room, and I was back in my body again. I had a breathing tube in my nose, and a nurse gave me a breathing thing that I had to blow into every so-many minutes. They kept me there the remainder of the day and night, but released me once the machine said that my respiration was high enough. I've told my story to my family and to anyone else who is interested. I've told them that if they are in a situation where they cannot breathe, the best thing to do is to try not to struggle and to just let go. Once you let go, it's easy. No pain or bad feelings. I used to fear drowning; always assuming it was the worst way to die. I know now that it is not. Death is not scary. It's not even painful at all. Everything feels good and right once you let it happen. 6/2/2020 Facebook post - Why are people racist on earth ? Many of you know about my Near-death-Experience due to arrythmia complication. While I was in heaven, I asked Jesus why are people racist on earth? This was my first question for obvious reasons. He looked at me with tremendous love, and in a very factual non-judgmental voice said, word for word: “It is because of their self-centeredness”. It had never crossed my mind that this could be the reason. But when you think of it, if you are over-focusing on yourself, you want to surround yourself only with people that look just like you and remind you of YOU. Anything different becomes a threat… A great way to transform that is to start having an interest in the other, forget about self for a moment and reach out to the different one in the crowd, get to know them and you will realize that they love just like you, they have a family who cares for them, they have hopes and dreams like you have, they have been hurt sometimes more than you have. They also participate in making this earth a better place to live. They can be sensitive at times because they have been hurt so often in their daily lives and they do aspire to be treated with fairness and included by all and at all times. Once we accept to open wider this heart of ours and let our mind rest, we deeply understand and realize we are all the same humans and Earthians, maybe with a stronger or milder melatonin level in these containers we call bodies. The violent treatments inflicted due to pre-conceived opinions of difference, based on physical perceptions, will then be irrelevant and equality will be a word we all believe in because we know it to be truly lived. PEACEFULLY standing for those who suffer is highly spiritual and a call to Unconditional Love for All ! Yvonne

out_of_body.separation_sensations_other: Felt pleasant while observing body shaking/bouncing; could also feel sensations while out of body ("I was aware that I was looking down on my body - but I could also feel.").

boundary_and_return.return_method_other_detail: Experience went black; later woke up during transfer to hospital room and was back in body.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Outpatient toe surgery; breathing tube removed and she was unable to breathe (later noted as 'arrythmia complication' in a 2020 Facebook post).

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Blackness/void followed by return to body; later (2020 Facebook post) reports being 'in heaven' and asking Jesus a question, but no detailed stage sequence is provided for that portion.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: OBE in hospital room (ceiling vantage) with resuscitation activity observed; then everything went black; then awakened back in body.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Later-added 6/2/2020 Facebook post describes being 'in heaven' and asking Jesus why people are racist; answer given: 'It is because of their self-centeredness.'

It's not even painful at all. Everything feels good and right once you let it happen.” / “It is because of their self-centeredness”.
